prompt: Which threads run a parallel stream's pipeline?

choices.text: A pool the stream creates and shuts down each time
choices.why: The pool is shared and lives as long as the program.

choices.text: A new thread created for each element
choices.why: Four threads handled 100,000 elements.

choices.text: Only the common pool's workers; `main` waits
choices.why: `main` processed 43,750 elements itself.

choices.text: The thread that called, plus the common pool's workers
choices.why: Right: `main` and `ForkJoinPool.commonPool-worker-N`.

prompt: On a machine with 4 processors, how many workers does the common pool have?
hint: One fewer, because the caller helps.

prompt: Why does a `LinkedList` make a poor source for a parallel stream?

choices.text: Its elements are always boxed
choices.why: Every `List` of objects holds references; that is not the issue.

choices.text: It cannot be streamed in parallel at all
choices.why: It can; it splits badly.

choices.text: It is not thread-safe, so the stream refuses it
choices.why: Reading from it is fine; nothing refuses it.

choices.text: Finding the middle means walking half of it
choices.why: Right.

prompt: `Primes.java` keeps the best of five runs for each version. Why?
hint: The first runs include something else.

choices.text: Five is the number of processors plus one
choices.why: The count of runs has nothing to do with processors.

choices.text: The parallel version gives a different answer each time
choices.why: Both printed 148933 every time.

choices.text: They include the JIT compiling the code
choices.why: Right: the cheapest correction for warm-up.

choices.text: `nanoTime` is wrong on the first call
choices.why: The clock is fine; the code being measured is still being compiled.

prompt: The parallel sum of a hundred small numbers took 50 µs against 14 sequential. What cost the difference?
hint: The arithmetic took about a microsecond.

choices.text: Adding numbers in a different order changes the result
choices.why: Both printed 4950.

choices.text: Boxing each number into an `Integer`
choices.why: `IntStream` does not box.

choices.text: Handing pieces to other threads and waiting
choices.why: Right: the overhead dwarfed the work.

choices.text: The common pool was busy with another program
choices.why: Each JVM has its own pool.

prompt: For a decision that matters, the lesson recommends OpenJDK's benchmark harness, called ___.
Ten parallel `forEach(shared::add)` runs on an `ArrayList`: some lost elements, one threw, three were right. What is the fix?

choices.text: Use `forEachOrdered` instead of `forEach`
choices.why: It orders the calls, and they still touch a shared list.

choices.text: A `synchronized` block around every call to `add`
choices.why: That works and serialises the work; the lesson's fix is not to share.

choices.text: Retry until a run comes out right
choices.why: Three came out right, and nothing tells you which ones.

choices.text: Let the stream build the list, with `toList()` or a collector
choices.why: Right: each thread gets its own container.

prompt: Why does the lesson call the three correct runs the worst of the three outcomes?

choices.text: A test that landed on one would pass
choices.why: Right: the bug hides.

choices.text: They were slower than the others
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: Their results were in the wrong order
choices.why: Only the size was checked, and it was right.

choices.text: They used more memory
choices.why: Memory is not the point either.

prompt: On a parallel stream, which returns the first match in source order?
hint: The other may return any match.

choices.text: `forEachOrdered`
choices.why: That returns nothing; it only visits the elements in order.

choices.text: `anyMatch`
choices.why: That answers yes or no.

choices.text: `findAny()`
choices.why: It returned 625601, whichever a thread found.

choices.text: `findFirst()`
choices.why: Right: it printed 0.

prompt: Match each call on a parallel stream with what it guarantees about order.

pairs.right: source order, by making threads wait

prompt: A parallel stream's lambda calls a slow web service. What else in the program suffers?

choices.text: Nothing: each parallel stream gets its own threads
choices.why: They all share the common pool.

choices.text: The garbage collector, which stops until the call returns
choices.why: The collector does not wait for network calls.

choices.text: Every other parallel stream, all left waiting for a worker
choices.why: Right: the waiting lambdas hold the pool's few workers.

choices.text: Only sequential streams, which lose their thread
choices.why: Sequential streams run on the caller's thread.

prompt: Which of these make a pipeline a good candidate for `parallel()`? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Expensive computation per element
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Lambdas that query a database
choices.why: No: they wait, and hold the pool's workers.

choices.text: Hundreds of thousands of elements
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Lambdas that add to a shared counter
choices.why: No: shared state.

choices.text: An `ArrayList` or an array as the source
choices.why: Yes: it splits evenly.

prompt: A colleague raises `java.util.concurrent.ForkJoinPool.common.parallelism` to speed up one slow pipeline. What does the lesson warn?

choices.text: The property is read-only
choices.why: It can be set when the JVM starts.

choices.text: The whole program shares that pool
choices.why: Right: a decision for everybody, not a tuning knob for one.

choices.text: It takes effect only for sequential streams
choices.why: It sizes the pool parallel streams use.

choices.text: It is ignored on machines with more than four processors
choices.why: It applies on any machine.

prompt: Put a parallel stream's work in order.
items: the spliterator cuts the source into pieces
the calling thread and the workers run the pipeline on the pieces

prompt: A pipeline of 40 elements with cheap lambdas got slower with `parallel()`. What should you do?

choices.text: Switch the source to a `LinkedList`
choices.why: That splits worse.

choices.text: Replace `toList()` with `forEach`
choices.why: The terminal operation is not the cost.

choices.text: Remove `parallel()`
choices.why: Right: the measurement decided.

choices.text: Add more workers to the common pool
choices.why: More threads make the overhead larger, not smaller.
